survey: A coral cluster on a seabed. A large pink branching coral grows up from behind a big slate-blue rock. Its thick trunk goes down behind the rock, and its branches fork in a believable way with rounded, pitted tips. Two orange branching corals stand behind the cluster, one on the left and one on the right. Their bases are hidden behind the rocks and the purple coral. A purple-magenta coral stands in front of the left side of the big rock, with its base hidden among the low rocks. A small red fan-shaped coral sits on the sand in front of the big rock. The tool's ellipses on two of its tips, at ratios 0.80 and 0.93, only fit rounded tips, which should not be perfect circles. Several flat grey-green stones sit on the sand around the base and cast contact shadows, so nothing floats. Every coral either sits on the ground or plausibly grows from behind a rock. There are no thin parts with loose ends, no parts passing through each other and no invented parts. The branching is simplified but organic and believable.
